response.title: What dehumidifier do I need for a finished basement where the only drain is a sink, so the water has to be pumped up?
response.answer:
For a finished basement where the only drain is a sink located higher than the dehumidifier, you need a dehumidifier with a built-in condensate pump.

The pump automatically pushes collected water through a small hose up to your sink, so you don't have to empty a bucket.

What I recommend

Look for these specifications:

Feature

	

Recommendation




Capacity

	

50 pints/day for most finished basements




Drainage

	

Built-in automatic condensate pump




Pump lift

	

At least 10–15 feet, depending on sink height




Humidity control

	

Adjustable humidistat




Target humidity

	

45–50% relative humidity




Restart

	

Automatic restart after power outages




Energy efficiency

	

ENERGY STAR certified

A 50-pint model is a good starting point for a typical 1,000–2,000 sq. ft. finished basement, although actual sizing depends on moisture levels and temperature.

You can also use a regular dehumidifier with a separate condensate pump, but an integrated model is simpler for this setup.

How high does the water need to be pumped? Is the sink in the basement, roughly 3–4 feet above the floor, or is it upstairs?

With those two details, I can recommend the right capacity and pump configuration without having you pay for more than you need.
